claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a uniform fcc matrix.
The as-built alloy contains microstructural heterogeneities arising from the additive-manufacturing process.
A controlled post-processing heat treatment can modify grain-boundary chemistry in this alloy.
A controlled post-processing heat treatment can modify the grain-boundary precipitate distribution in this alloy.
Heat-treatment-induced grain-boundary modifications can reduce diffusion pathways for oxidizing species.
Grain-boundary diffusion is active during oxidizing exposure around 900°C.
Exposure around 900°C can occur without provoking major phase transformations in the alloy.
The proposed treatment promotes coarsening or stabilization of grain-boundary precipitates.
Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion pathways that accelerate oxidation.
Coarsening or stabilization of grain-boundary precipitates reduces the ingress rate of oxidizing species along grain boundaries.
The proposed grain-boundary modification can preserve the overall fcc matrix.
Preservation of the fcc matrix supports the alloy's strength and fatigue performance.
Under identical oxidizing exposure, the annealed alloy will have a shallower oxidation penetration depth than the as-built alloy.
Under identical oxidizing exposure, the annealed alloy will have a lower oxidation rate than the as-built alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain its mechanical integrity during the proposed exposure.
At temperatures up to approximately 950°C, oxidation can remain diffusion-controlled without significant phase transformation or deleterious grain growth.
